subject.title: Codex turn fails with generic Telegram fallback when invalid image tool model is configured, leaving child agent orphaned on full stdout pipe

question: Should the remaining fix be limited to explicit media-model preflight plus Telegram diagnostics first, or should it also redesign Codex stdout/stderr log redirection and child cleanup in the same change?
rationale: The evidence shows current source gaps, but the right owner boundary spans config validation, channel fallback UX, and Codex lifecycle behavior; choosing that scope is a maintainer product and reliability decision.

options.title: Preflight and diagnose first
options.body: Define the first fix as explicit media-model validation or clear tool errors plus a Telegram error id/log pointer, then require live proof before deeper Codex log-redirection work.

options.title: Full lifecycle hardening now
options.body: Include per-run Codex stdout/stderr log redirection and parent-failure cleanup in the same work, accepting a broader process-lifecycle review surface.

options.title: Wait for live repro
options.body: Keep this in needs-live-repro until a maintainer reproduces the orphaned pipe path on current main before choosing implementation scope.

recommendation.title: Preflight and diagnose first
recommendation.body: Define the first fix as explicit media-model validation or clear tool errors plus a Telegram error id/log pointer, then require live proof before deeper Codex log-redirection work.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history spans config validation, media generation, Telegram dispatch, and Codex lifecycle seams, and this owner appears across all of those areas.
